title: International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy Nutrition
excerpt: Oats, Greek yogurt, lentils, low-mercury salmon, eggs, leafy greens, and citrus — practical ways to build balanced plates
content:
## Introduction
When it comes to pregnancy nutrition, choosing the right foods is crucial for the health and well-being of both mother and baby. In this article, we'll explore international pantry staples that are good for pregnancy, helping you build a balanced and varied diet.

## International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy
Here are some international pantry staples that are good for pregnancy:
* Oats: rich in fiber, supporting digestive health and reducing the risk of constipation.
* Greek yogurt: rich in calcium, supporting bone and tooth development for the baby.
* Lentils: rich in iron, supporting blood development and preventing anemia.
* Low-mercury salmon: rich in omega-3 fatty acids, supporting brain and eye development for the baby.
* Eggs: rich in protein, supporting muscle and tissue development for the baby.
* Leafy greens and citrus: rich in vitamins and minerals, supporting immune function and preventing disease.

## Building Balanced Plates for Pregnancy
To build a balanced and varied diet, you can combine these pantry staples into your daily meals. Here are some suggestions:
* Breakfast: oatmeal with Greek yogurt and fruit.
* Lunch: salad with leafy greens, lentils, and low-mercury salmon.
* Dinner: scrambled eggs with leafy greens and citrus.

## Food Safety During Pregnancy
When it comes to pregnancy, food safety is crucial to prevent illness and protect the health of both mother and baby. Here are some key considerations:
* Avoid eating raw or undercooked foods, such as sushi or raw eggs.
* Avoid eating foods high in mercury, such as shark or swordfish.
* Avoid eating foods that may contain listeria, such as soft cheese or deli meats.

## Conclusion
International pantry staples can help you build a balanced and varied diet during pregnancy. However, food safety is crucial to prevent illness and protect the health of both mother and baby.
